board_rules: Parallelism only between tasks with disjoint files_expected and satisfied depends_on.
One commit per implementable task, message format: '<task-id>: <short description>'.
Definition of done per task: task-scoped tests pass, lint clean, diff limited to files_expected, evidence recorded in the task's 'validation_result' field.

License guard (ICEBERG_CATALOG_PLAN.md §2, DATASETS_DESIGN.md §2): implement from the Apache Iceberg spec and lakeFS public docs only. Never copy from lakeFS Enterprise code or upstream >= 1.87 (BSL). Cite the spec URL in the PR.
Spike tasks (type=spike) deliver a written note file, not product code; they may be superseded by a later task's findings, which must be recorded in the superseding task's notes.
Any task that changes the wire format must update /v1/config 'endpoints' in the same commit (ICEBERG_CATALOG_PLAN.md §2.1: clients only call advertised endpoints).

autocommit.precondition: validation command for the task exited 0 and its tail is in validation_result
autocommit.scope: git add exactly files_expected; never stage unrelated work. tasks.json and agent-progress.txt are committed only by the planning commit and by D1.
autocommit.on_failure: do not commit; leave status in_progress, write the failing output into validation_result.details, stop and report
never: amend or force-push a commit belonging to another task
commit generated code without the generator change that produced it

work_waves.comment: Advisory scheduling that respects depends_on and the max-5 cap. Workers may pick any 'ready' task whose deps are done and whose files_expected do not collide with another in_progress task.

tasks.commit_message: I6-1: materialise table and namespace items into datasets
notes: Payoff of §6.3: without staged file entries a table item cannot be materialised at all.

Gate: IcebergEnabled (pkg/datasets) reads the iceberg.enabled key pkg/icebergcatalog reads (IcebergEnabledKey is pinned to icebergcatalog.ConfigKey by a test). Disabled keeps the existing '(501)' problem at data[i].type, so unsupportedCheck still answers 501.

Placement: a table/namespace item copies the source's reserved _lakefs_iceberg/ keys unchanged, so the dataset answers /iceberg/api at <ds>.<ref>.<ns>.<table>. Its target must therefore equal the catalog path (<ns>/<table> or <ns>), which also makes the §5.2 rule-3 overlap check answer 'this would materialise twice'.

Key ownership (decided here, documented in openIcebergItem): a namespace marker belongs to the namespace item that covers it and is never copied by a table item, otherwise two sibling table items (a valid definition) would collide on the same marker key and fail the §6.4 merge. Regression: TestPublishSiblingTableItems.
Subtree semantics: a namespace item copies its own markers plus every nested marker, table pointer and table file tree; ancestors' markers are left to a namespace item that covers them.
A missing table/namespace at the pinned ref is a *ValidationError naming the item (400), not a 5xx.

End-to-end proof: TestPublishedTableReadableThroughCatalog reads the published table with icebergcatalog.Store.GetTable on the dataset repo at the version tag (the catalog computes the pointer path itself); TestPublishNamespaceItem does the same with GetNamespace.
Out of scope here (I6-2): api/datasets.yml + pkg/datasets/apigen still document table/namespace as 'answered with 501'; authz SourceObjectArn still checks the whole repository for a table item.

SourceReadNode(table item) = And[catalog:ReadTable, catalog:ReadTableData] on CatalogTableArn(repo, ns, table) - the pair /iceberg/api itself checks (ICEBERG_CATALOG_PLAN.md §7.2). The fs:ListObjects/fs:ReadObject pair is gone for table items because the catalog does not require it; fs:ReadRepository is still checked first by CheckSourceRepositories and SourceReader.CheckObject still authorizes every entry the materialiser reads.

New SourceTableArn(item) (catalog ARN + ok) is the single builder of that ARN; it reports ok=false for a missing/empty descriptor, so SourceReadNode falls back to the whole-repository object glob (fail closed). A namespace item keeps that fallback: it covers every table below it, so no single catalog ARN describes it.
itemSourcePath now names a table as <ns>.<table> and a namespace as <ns>, so a 403 names the catalog object instead of an empty path (TestSourceItemNameReserved).

The ARN uses the definition's dotted namespace unchanged: validate.icebergNamespaceSeparator is '.', which is also Namespace.Dotted(), the form icebergcatalog builds its ARNs from - no conversion; pinned by TestSourceReadNode/TestSourceTableArn.
